title: parthenium integrifolium var. auriculatum
intro: Parthenium integrifolium var. auriculatum, commonly known as Wild Feverfew, is a plant species that belongs to the sunflower family. It has been traditionally used for its health benefits, including reducing fever, relieving headaches and migraines, and treating digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of Wild Feverfew include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antipyretic properties, making it a potential natural remedy for various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of Wild Feverfew include sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
